answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one licensed coral-reef survey transect, where a diver counts ivory coral colonies by hand and logs every dive beside a pressed yarrow specimen from the shore station garden. Random spot-checks summon the diver to that exact reef within a day, and one diver cannot survey two transects at once. The survey license fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real reef, another trained diver, another season of dives, and twice the prior fee.
